results.action: skip the broad pitch; use it as social proof
results.one_sentence: A #1 Product of the Day is great validation and good for your own channels, but Product Hunt wins are common and won't earn a standalone story from tech reporters without traction, funding, or a differentiated angle.
A top-3 finish with 466 upvotes plus a generic 'future of human-AI collaboration' framing is not a story; the angle is a crowded buzzword and there's no data or differentiation to hang a pitch on.

results.action: skip the press pitch; lean on dev communities
results.one_sentence: A clipboard utility with 225 upvotes is a nice niche tool best promoted in developer communities and newsletters, not via reporter pitches, since there's no notability, data, or exclusive.

results.action: hold until you can verify the numbers and name a partner
results.one_sentence: 'First in-chat brokerage trading' is a genuinely interesting and pitchable angle, but unverified user counts and an unnamed brokerage partner make it risky and likely to get killed by skeptical fintech reporters until you can substantiate it.

NVIDIA's first data-center CPU purpose-built for agentic AI, with hard specs and a roster of marquee partners including Anthropic, OpenAI, Oracle and NYSE, is genuinely major industry news that enterprise-tech and chip reporters will want.

The Anthropic IPO is a huge story and a builder who depends on frontier-model economics has real standing to offer a fresh angle, so this is a credible reactive-commentary play if you move fast and bring a genuinely non-obvious point of view.
A fast-casual chain with no AI product and no relevant expertise commenting on an AI IPO has zero standing and would look opportunistic and tone-deaf, so don't do it.
A local-SEO agency has no meaningful connection to a frontier-model megaround, and the 'AI is our space' justification is keyword-overlap reaching that journalists will dismiss.
Newsjacking an active E. coli outbreak where people are sick to sell meal-kit subscriptions is exploitative and will read as callous; this is a brand-safety landmine, not an opportunity.
The Alphabet compute story broke over a week ago with declining velocity and the client brings no new data or contrarian angle, so the timing window has closed and a late me-too comment won't land.

A clinical-stage gene-therapy biotech directly governed by brand-new FDA guidance, with a named CMO who can explain regulatory and patient-access implications, has strong standing and a timely expert angle reporters covering the guidance will want.

During a 37-million-pound recall, an independent food-safety lab with first-party detection data and a named scientist offering a sober, non-promotional explainer is exactly the credible expert source reporters seek, so move quickly while the story is hot.

SoftBank's record 5GW France investment is major infrastructure news, and a cooling/power-density vendor with first-party efficiency data and a named engineer has a legitimate, differentiated 'realities of 5GW' angle that trade and infra reporters will value.
A 4.00% CD APY that merely matches the market with no exclusive data or trend angle is not newsworthy; this belongs in your own marketing, not a reporter pitch.

results.action: pitch ahead of the FOMC meeting
results.one_sentence: A consumer-lending fintech with first-party application/refi data and a named chief economist has a genuinely useful, data-backed angle into the June Fed decision that personal-finance and markets reporters can use, especially if pitched before the June 16-17 meeting.

A cluster of EV battery recalls creates real reporter demand for technical context, and a BMS/EV-safety firm with first-party failure-analysis data and a named engineer can credibly explain why these faults happen without exploiting harm, making for a solid expert-source play.
